bib.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

question: Which choices of architecture, pre-training objective, unlabeled data, transfer approach and scale matter most for transfer learning in NLP when every task is cast as text-to-text, and how far does scaling them go?
contributions: A unified text-to-text framework for all NLP tasks
A systematic empirical comparison of architectures, objectives, data sets, transfer approaches and scaling
The C4 data set (about 750 GB of cleaned Common Crawl English text)
T5 models up to 11B parameters with state-of-the-art results on many benchmarks
Release of code, C4 and pre-trained model weights

method.summary: Every task is cast as text in, text out with a task prefix, and one encoder-decoder Transformer is trained with maximum likelihood. A baseline (220M params, span-style denoising on C4, 2^35 tokens, then per-task fine-tuning) is varied one factor at a time. The best settings are combined and scaled to T5 Small/Base/Large/3B/11B pre-trained on about 1T tokens.
method.task: text-to-text transfer learning: denoising pre-training then fine-tuning on GLUE, SuperGLUE, CNN/DM, SQuAD, WMT En-De/Fr/Ro

datasets.name: C4 (Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus)
datasets.split: never repeated in baseline (2^35 tokens used)
datasets.source: Common Crawl web-extracted text from April 2019, released in TensorFlow Datasets
datasets.preprocessing: Keep lines ending in terminal punctuation; drop pages with fewer than 3 sentences, lines with fewer than 5 words, pages with bad words, lorem ipsum or '{'; remove lines with 'Javascript' or policy strings; strip citation markers; dedupe three-sentence spans; langdetect English with probability at least 0.99

datasets.name: C4 variants (unfiltered 6.1TB, RealNews-like 35GB, WebText-like 17GB, Wikipedia 16GB, Wikipedia+TBC 20GB)
datasets.source: Common Crawl, Wikipedia (TFDS), Toronto Books Corpus
datasets.preprocessing: WebText-like uses 12 months of Common Crawl (Aug 2018 to Jul 2019) filtered to Reddit-score>=3 URLs

datasets.name: GLUE (WNLI never trained on) and SuperGLUE (plus DPR)
datasets.split: validation sets in all experiments except Sec 3.7 (test via benchmark servers)
datasets.source: GLUE and SuperGLUE as distributed; constituent tasks concatenated into one task for fine-tuning
datasets.preprocessing: Task prefix text; STS-B rounded to nearest 0.2 and written as string; Winograd tasks recast as referent noun prediction

datasets.name: CNN/Daily Mail
datasets.source: non-anonymized version of See et al. 2017

datasets.name: SQuAD
datasets.split: validation set throughout (test server could not run largest models)
datasets.preprocessing: question and context fed in, answer generated token by token

datasets.name: WMT En-De, En-Fr, En-Ro
datasets.split: validation newstest2013 (De), newstest2014 (Fr), WMT 2016 val (Ro); test newstest2014/2015/2016
datasets.source: De: News Commentary v13, Common Crawl, Europarl v7; Fr: 2015 standard data; Ro: WMT 2016

models.name: Baseline / T5-Base
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer, pre-LN (layer norm without bias), relative position scalars (32 buckets, logarithmic to offset 128), shared embedding/softmax
models.vocab: 32,000 wordpieces (trained on 10 parts English C4 to 1 part each German, French, Romanian)

training.objective: Maximum likelihood with teacher forcing and cross-entropy. Baseline: i.i.d. denoising, 15% of tokens dropped, consecutive spans replaced by unique sentinel tokens, target is the dropped spans. Final T5: span corruption, mean span length 3, 15% corrupted
training.lr: pre-train 0.01 constant for first 10^4 steps then inverse square root decay; fine-tune constant 0.001
training.batch_size: 128 sequences of length 512 (about 2^16 = 65,536 tokens incl. packing) baseline; 2^11 sequences for final T5 pre-training; 8 sequences for per-task GLUE/SuperGLUE fine-tuning in Sec 3.7
training.steps: baseline pre-train 2^19 = 524,288, fine-tune 2^18 = 262,144; final T5 pre-train 1M steps
training.tokens: baseline 2^35 about 34B; final T5 about 1 trillion
training.hardware: Cloud TPU Pod slices (TPU v3, pod = 1,024 chips), Mesh TensorFlow model and data parallelism
training.seeds: baseline trained 10 times from scratch (different init and data shuffle) to estimate std dev; other variants single run

other.checkpointing: save every 5,000 steps (1,000 for per-task GLUE/SuperGLUE in 3.7), report best validation checkpoint
other.multitask_mix_sizes_final: artificial unlabeled size 710,000 Small, 2,620,000 Base, 8,660,000 Large, 33,500,000 3B, 133,000,000 11B; En-Fr and En-De capped at 1M examples
other.mixing: examples-proportional r_m=min(e_m,K)/sum min(e_n,K); temperature-scaled with K=2^21

inference.decoding: greedy for all ablations; beam search width 4, length penalty alpha=0.6 for WMT and CNN/DM in Sec 3.7
inference.samples: baseline 10 training runs; single run per variant
inference.prompting: task prefix such as 'translate English to German:', 'cola sentence:', 'summarize:'

other.invalid_output: output not in label set counted wrong

limits: Coordinate-ascent design misses interactions between factors (authors concede)
Variants other than the baseline were run once; variance borrowed from 10 baseline runs
Baseline is small (220M, 34B tokens); effects may differ for larger models (authors say bigger models may overfit small pre-training sets more)
English-only pre-training; no SOTA on any WMT task
Validation sets used for nearly all comparisons; SQuAD final reported on validation
Low-resource tasks (CoLA, CB, COPA) have high variance, making GLUE and SuperGLUE averages noisy
Table 10 appears to print the d=128 row twice for d=2048
Model sizes, SOTA claims as of October 24th, 2019 have dated
Authors state it is not proposing new methods but a survey and comparison
